tools.name: sql_impact
tools.label: SQL impact (live catalog trace)
tools.description: Read-only live impact trace of ONE SQL object on the contract's default dev/test sql_targets entry: three fixed parameterized catalog queries for downstream dependents, upstream references and columns. An unavailable section means the target could not be asked; an empty downstream list means none visible to this principal in this database, never 'could not look'. Accepts only `object`.
tools.promptSnippet: Live catalog trace of one SQL object's dependents, references and columns
promptGuidelines: Before planning or editing a live SQL object, call sql_impact with its name, then data_doc lineage for the same object when built docs exist, and report drift between them. Metadata only: use fabric_sql_query for rows.

tools.name: catalog_snapshot
tools.label: Catalog snapshot
tools.description: Committed dev catalog snapshot: one file per table, view, procedure and function. command=status (default): exists and how old. command=snapshot: read the dev/test catalog read-only (never production) and rewrite the folder to commit.
tools.promptSnippet: Committed dev catalog snapshot: status or refresh
promptGuidelines: Read the object's snapshot file before writing SQL; if the snapshot is missing or stale, offer catalog_snapshot (command="snapshot") once.

tools.name: schema_compare
tools.label: Schema compare
tools.description: Read-only compare of two schemas (sql_targets entries, the snapshot or a repo's .sql files) with an ordered promotion script. Writes report.md and deploy.sql under .coop/schema-compare, never runs them.
tools.promptSnippet: Compare dev, prod or repo schemas; ordered promotion script, nothing applied
promptGuidelines: To move SQL changes between environments, call schema_compare first; deploy.sql is the person's to run. Pass only the choices the user names for this run: the project file holds the client's defaults.

tools.name: fabric_sql_query
tools.label: Fabric SQL Query (pyodbc fallback)
tools.description: Governed pyodbc read of one bounded SELECT against the contract's default sql_targets entry, or the entry `environment` names (dev, test or prod, to compare them, or <env>@<set> for a second engine under sql_targets.named such as dev@serverless), (Azure SQL, Fabric SQL database, Synapse serverless, Fabric Warehouse/Lakehouse), or the canonical Fabric SQL target without sql_targets. When a managed fabric-sqlendpoint MCP tool exists, attempt it first and call fabric_sql_query only after that actual attempt fails (unavailable/missing, authentication, timeout, connection, transport). Never use it for SQL/business/query rejection. Accepts no target, server, credential, or token fields.
tools.promptSnippet: Post-MCP-failure pyodbc fallback for one approval-gated bounded Fabric SELECT TOP read
promptGuidelines: With a managed fabric-sqlendpoint MCP server, attempt it first; call fabric_sql_query only after an actual unavailable/authentication/timeout/connection/transport/tool-missing failure, never for SQL/business/query rejection, and never cascade automatically. Direct sql_targets kinds (Azure SQL, Fabric SQL database, Synapse) have no MCP server: fabric_sql_query is the live read route.
Use only one plain SELECT with a literal TOP bound; mutations, batches, cross-database names, and unbounded reads are rejected before authentication or connection.

tools.name: standards_check
tools.label: Standards check (fresh look)
tools.description: Read-only second look at files you changed: a separate model request sees only the change and the standards.
tools.promptSnippet: Fresh standards check of your change
promptGuidelines: Before presenting a SQL, DAX or model change, call standards_check once with the changed files; fix its findings or state why not.

tools.name: bpa_review
tools.label: Tabular Editor BPA
tools.description: Run Tabular Editor BPA against semantic-model files using built-in or configured rules and return findings as JSON. Advisory only — never edits model files.
tools.promptSnippet: Check semantic models with Tabular Editor BPA (advisory, JSON output)
promptGuidelines: Use bpa_review to check semantic models before proposing or reviewing changes.
Treat results as advisory; summarize findings by severity.

tools.name: data_doc
tools.label: Data Documentation
tools.description: Understand and document whatever SQL and/or Power BI source is available with coop-data-doc. Commands: 'scan' (default) writes the lineage graph (graph.json); 'build' also writes per-object Markdown docs and a portal, indexed by manifest.json; 'check' is a CI staleness gate; 'lineage' lists ONE object's upstream inputs, downstream dependents and relationships; 'impact' lists every downstream object that changed source files feed. Any stage of source coverage is valid. Without a coop-data-doc.yml or built graph, proceed without it (an aid, not a gate): never 'scan' or 'build' unasked; name /setup-docs only if the user asks. Outputs are committable; source is never touched.
tools.promptSnippet: SQL+Power BI estate: lineage graph, one object's up/downstream, what a change feeds
promptGuidelines: When built lineage docs exist, call data_doc with command='lineage', object='<name>' before changing a SQL object, DAX measure or semantic model. Don't reconstruct lineage by hand; without built docs, sql_impact is the check.
After editing SQL, DAX or model source files and before presenting the change, call data_doc with command='impact', files=[the changed paths] and report every downstream object it lists.
Default to 'lineage' and 'impact' (read-only); 'scan' or 'build' only when the user asks. Read the focused per-object Markdown via manifest.json, not the whole tree.
Without a coop-data-doc.yml or built graph ('no built graph'), proceed without it; no scan, build or /setup-docs unless the user asks.

message.content: An observed lineage graph is available under data-docs: graph.json. Its coverage may be partial or unknown; empty lineage does not prove zero impact. BEFORE analyzing or changing any SQL object, DAX measure, or semantic model, look up its observed up/downstream impact via the data_doc tool (command="lineage", object="<name>"). Use the graph as it is; do not run data_doc build on your own. If the graph looks stale, say so once; the user decides whether to rebuild it.
